notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the source pages.

I tried to open five pages in one batch: Enduring Word on Jeremiah 32, Precept Austin's Jeremiah 32 page, the Bible Hub commentary pages for verses 7 and 17, and the NET Bible notes on Jeremiah 32. The request went out, but my code failed while handling the results, so none of the page text came through. The tool then told me I had no more searches or fetches left for this turn. My other tools have no internet access, so I couldn't try another way.

Your rules say to use only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. That means I have nothing I can honestly put in the notes. Writing them from what I already know about Jeremiah 32 would break that rule, so I haven't.

If you ask again in a new message, I can start over with a fresh set of lookups and do it in this order:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Jeremiah 32, the Bible Hub verse pages (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry and others) for verses 1–22, and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** sites from each tradition on the key verses, such as the right of redemption in verses 7–8, the "nothing is too difficult" line in verse 17, and the iniquity of the fathers in verse 18. Sources would include Wesley's notes, Spurgeon's sermons, Ligonier, Desiring God and the Lutheran sites.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible translator notes, Bible Odyssey for the siege dates and the practice of storing deeds in clay jars, and the Catholic and Orthodox sites. I'd add popular modern teaching only if a site actually discusses these verses.

To save fetches, you could also tell me which part matters most, for example verses 6–15 (the field purchase) or 16–22 (the prayer), and I'll start there.
